sheets.note: Leningrad front from the Gulf of Finland to the Neva and Schlüsselburg: as on the map of 30 November (sheet 1258535), the same course as on 1 January 1942
the Tikhvin salient (Tikhvin taken 8 November 1941), with Group Boeckmann before Volkhov and the Volkhov bridgeheads at Gruzino: drawn after the corps fronts on sheet 1258535
the Volkhov, Lake Ilmen, the Lovat and the Valdai hills to Lake Seliger: the same course as on 1 January 1942 (overlay checked)

Kalinin, the Moscow Sea, the Yakhroma bridgehead on the Moscow–Volga canal, Krasnaya Polyana, Istra, the Nara, the Oka at Aleksin, the ring round Tula, the advance on Kashira, Venev and Mikhailov, Yefremov, Livny and Tim: drawn after the corps fronts of Army Groups Centre and South on sheet 1258535
Belgorod, Kharkov, the Donets and the Mius: the same course as on 1 January 1942 (overlay checked on sheets 1258535 and 1258537; the Germans left Rostov on 29 November and fell back to the Mius)

pockets.name: Sevastopol
pockets.note: Fortress area besieged since November 1941 (Lage Ost: Festung Sewastopol)

pockets.name: Oranienbaum bridgehead
pockets.note: Coastal bridgehead west of Leningrad, held throughout the siege

sheets.note: Leningrad front: as on the map of 31 October (sheet 1436178)
the XXXIX Panzer Corps on the way to Tikhvin (Budogoshch and Malaya Vishera taken on 23 October 1941): drawn after the corps positions on the map
the Volkhov, Lake Ilmen, the Lovat and the Valdai hills to Lake Seliger: the same course as on 30 November

Kalinin, Volokolamsk, the Mozhaisk line at Ruza and Dorokhovo, the Nara and Protva, Aleksin and the first assault on Tula (30 October), then the flank of the 2nd Panzer Army along the Tula–Orel road and the 2nd Army before Kursk: drawn after the corps positions on the map, which shows the Soviet side mostly as unit symbols
Belgorod, east of Kharkov (taken 24 October), the Donets and the Mius at Taganrog (taken 17 October): the sheet ends at Kharkov; south of it the line is that of 30 November

pockets.name: Southern and eastern Crimea
pockets.note: The 11th Army broke through at Ishun on 28 October 1941; the Coastal Army and the 51st Army fell back to Sevastopol and to Kerch (Simferopol fell on 1 November, Feodosia on 3 November, Kerch on 16 November)

pockets.name: Oranienbaum bridgehead
pockets.note: Coastal bridgehead west of Leningrad, held throughout the siege

sheets.note: the map of 30 June (sheets 1024489, 1024490) shows the German divisions and corps (blue) and the Soviet ones (red) without a drawn line; the line is taken along the forward German positions: Riga and the Dvina with the bridgeheads at Jekabpils and Daugavpils, Glubokoye, Minsk (taken 28 June), Bobruisk (2nd Panzer Group, 28 June), Slutsk, the Pripyat marshes, Rovno and Ostrog (1st Panzer Group), Brody, Lviv (taken 30 June), Drohobych, the Carpathian and Prut borders (Hungary and Romania not yet attacking)

pockets.name: Bialystok–Minsk pocket
pockets.note: 3rd, 10th and 13th Armies encircled between Bialystok and Minsk (closed 28 June; the remnants surrendered by 9 July); the map marks them "Feindreste" and "Versprengte"

sheets.note: the first day of Barbarossa: the map of the evening of 22 June (sheet 1024543) shows no line but the German divisions and corps (blue) a day beyond the border; the line is drawn along their forward positions: Kretinga and Palanga, Tauragė and the Dubysa, Marijampolė, the Neman bridges of the 3rd Panzer Group at Alytus and Merkinė, the outskirts of Grodno and Augustów, the border of the Bialystok salient (where the 4th and 9th Armies had barely crossed), the Bug with Brest fortress encircled, the 2nd Panzer Group towards Kobryn and Pruzhany, Volodymyr-Volynskyi, Sokal and Radekhiv, Rava-Ruska and Jaworów, and the San at Przemyśl
the Carpathians and the Prut: the 1940 border, not crossed on 22 June (Hungary and Romania had not yet attacked; the map marks only bridgeheads on the Prut)

1941-06-22.adjustments: Brest fortress, which held out until 29 June (the last defenders until late July), is too small for a piece of its own (under 30 km²) and is left out.

sheets.note: the map of 31 July (sheets 1024599, 1024600) shows the German divisions and corps (blue) and the Soviet ones (red) but rarely a drawn line; the line is taken along the forward German positions: Pärnu and Tartu in Estonia, Lake Peipus, the Luga bridgeheads, Shimsk and the Shelon west of Staraya Russa, west of Velikiye Luki (retaken by the Red Army on 21 July), Nevel and Velizh, the Vop at Yartsevo, the Yelnya salient, Krichev and Propoisk, west of Rogachev and Zhlobin, Mozyr and the Korosten fortified area, the Irpen before Kiev, Bila Tserkva and the encirclement at Uman, and the Dniester to its mouth

pockets.name: Smolensk pocket
pockets.note: 16th and 20th Armies cut off north of the Dnieper between Smolensk and Yartsevo (closed 27 July 1941; broke out across the Solovyovo crossing by 4 August)

sheets.note: the map of 31 August (sheets 1024690, 1024691): the line along the forward German units: the coast at Koporye, Krasnogvardeysk, Tosno and Mga (taken 30 August), the Volkhov from Chudovo to Novgorod, the Lovat, Kholm, Toropets and Velikiye Luki (taken 26-29 August), Belyi, the Vop, the Yelnya salient, the Desna from Zhukovka to Novgorod-Seversky (2nd Panzer Group turning south), Chernigov, the Okuninovo bridgehead north of Kiev, the Dnieper from Kiev to Kremenchug and the Dnepropetrovsk bridgehead, Zaporozhye, Kakhovka and the Dnieper estuary

pockets.name: Moonsund islands
pockets.note: Saaremaa, Muhu and Hiiumaa held by the Red Army until 5 and 21 October 1941 (Operation Beowulf)

pockets.name: Odessa
pockets.note: Separate Coastal Army besieged by the Romanian 4th Army from 8 August 1941; evacuated by sea, the city fell on 16 October

sheets.note: the map of 30 September (sheets 1024739, 1024740), the day Operation Typhoon began on the southern wing: the siege ring at Leningrad and Shlisselburg (8 September), the Volkhov, the Lovat and Demyansk (8 September), Lake Seliger, Andreapol, Belyi, the Vop, Yelnya (retaken by the Red Army on 6 September), Roslavl and the Desna, Trubchevsk, the 2nd Panzer Group at Glukhov and Shostka, Romny and Lokhvitsa (Kiev pocket destroyed 26 September), Sumy, Poltava and Krasnograd, Dnepropetrovsk, Zaporozhye, the Nogai steppe west of Melitopol and Perekop (taken 26-28 September), with Crimea behind the Ishun line Soviet
